Definition: to be right (i.e. correct); reciprocal, to argue; causatively, to decide, justify or convict
BiblicalUsage: Yâkach is the word for arguing a case, deciding what is right, and calling someone to account. God Himself invites Israel to reason together with Him, though their sins are as scarlet, and Job desires to reason with God rather than with men who offer him empty comfort. The word also carries the work of the judge, as when Hezekiah asks the LORD to reprove the words of Rabshakeh, and of the arbiter who stands between two parties to decide between them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God is not afraid of our hardest questions, because He invites us to reason with Him. My position is that faith is not the absence of argument but the willingness to bring the argument to God and let Him decide it. And I hold that the God who reasons with sinners is the same God who justifies them, so I need not fear the verdict when I come to Him honestly.
